accuracy.evidence: Checked against the National Curriculum in England 2013, Year 6 Light (the three statutory statements on straight-line travel, seeing by emitted or reflected light, and shadow shape are quoted exactly) and the Association for Science Education / Primary Science Teaching Trust guidance on ray diagrams. Shadow sizes use similar triangles from a point source: height = card x (torch-to-screen)/(torch-to-card); the lab computes tall(x) = CARD*(SX-TX)/(x-TX) and items p3, p5, m6 use 2x, 3x and 4x for a card at a half, a third and a quarter of the distance, all recomputed. Point-source shadows are upright and enlarged, as drawn. The lesson says light 'appears to' travel in straight lines in the adult text, matching the curriculum wording.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets misconceptions documented by Osborne et al. (1990) SPACE Research Report 'Light' and Driver et al. (1994) Making Sense of Secondary Science: vision as rays from the eye ('eyes', prediction 2, the eye-first tap feedback, p2, m2), seeing without light reaching the eye (m5, 'glow'), light bending round objects ('bend', prediction 1, p1), shadows as reflections ('reflect', m4), and shadows shrinking as the object nears the light ('smaller', prediction 4, m3). Each wrong path in the 'How do we see?' step gets its own message.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagray is about the straight-line model itself: the three-holed-card experiment with a draggable middle card, a tap-to-build ray path that rejects eye-first and book-first paths, shaped cards whose edge rays trace a matching silhouette, a slider that changes shadow size by similar triangles, and a predict-then-reveal shadow edge. flagshadow (ages 4-5) only finds light sources and makes a teddy's shadow appear; flagshine is reflection from surfaces. Max 6-shingle similarity with any other lab is under 4%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers each idea before the text confirms it: nudging the middle card off line visibly stops the beam at that card; starting a ray at the eye is refused with the reason; the edge rays drawn past each card land exactly at the silhouette's top and bottom; sliding the card shows the ratio climb to over 2x near the torch and fall to 1.1x near the screen; in the predict step the learner must picture the straight edge ray before switching on, and a miss says whether the mark was too low or too high.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'yes, light bends round' (the beam stops at the off-line card), 'light leaves my eyes and hits the book' (the eye-first path is rejected), 'a round blob' for the star card (the star silhouette appears), and 'it gets smaller' when the card moves towards the torch (the ratio grows to 2x and beyond).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions and ten distinct feedback messages naming the slip, for example 'Eyes do not send out light. Light comes from a source, bounces off things, and enters the eye', 'A shadow is where light is blocked, not a reflection', 'Light does not bend round objects. Straight rays that just miss the edge make the outline', 'Closer to the torch, the toy blocks a wider spread of rays, so the shadow gets bigger', and 'Light travels one way: from the source, then to the object, then to the eye'.

readability.evidence: Kid text is short sentences with the Year 6 terms light source, ray, reflect, shadow, straight line; validate_lessons passes the kid and adult readability limits (kid FK 2.4, adult 7.6 by the repo's fk_grade). Lab step text is one or two sentences per step and canvas labels are single words (lamp, book, eye, card, screen) or a short status line.

no_filler.evidence: Gate finds no filler phrases. Each kid paragraph teaches one point (straight lines; how we see; shadow outline; shadow size). Items apply the model rather than recall it: p3, p5 and m6 use the distance ratio, m8 works backwards from a shadow to a distance ratio, m9 explains the laser-in-smoke evidence. Every hint points to the reasoning and every explanation gives the reason.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark: the three cards, eye and torch fit with the drag handle 13 px radius above the middle card and a 36 px wide hit zone; the lamp label moved down so it no longer touches the status chip; the screen panel holds the full star, house and rabbit silhouettes; buttons wrap to two rows; status chips shrink their font to fit 390 px without clipping. Desktop 1200 px also checked.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button: Middle card up/down and Line it up, lamp/book/eye/Clear to build the path, Next card, Closer to torch / Closer to screen, Mark higher / Mark lower / Switch on. The canvas aria-label is rewritten with each outcome, challenge feedback is a polite live region, and walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
